articles.title: Saros Gets Boss Rush And Tons Of Difficulty Options With Zenith Update
articles.summary: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been waiting for the right time to play it--or to play it again--then developer Housemarque has some good news.
body: First up, the boss rush. Dubbed "Overlord Rush," the mode comes with its own dedicated leaderboards and tasks you with taking out a series of the game's bosses. Rather than starting on the first boss and fighting uninterrupted to the very end, they're divided into separate "sets" that each contain three fights. Overlord Rush is available via the Primary robot in the main hub area.

The new settings and difficulty modifiers, meanwhile, allow you to both reduce and increase the game's challenge, customizing it to fit your preferences. The "Slow Game Speed" setting lets you slow down the entire game so you have more time to react to projectiles, and you can tweak exactly how much it slows down and even if you want it to turn on automatically when combat starts. An "Auto-fire" setting also eliminates the need to actually pull the trigger when you aim, which can be handy when you're primarily focused on dodging incoming attacks. You can think of it almost like a Vampire Survivors-style tool.
points: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026.

articles.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Biddy Blas Is Voiced By A Sinister Circus Ringmaster Pro Wrestler, And This Makes Sense
articles.summary: Star Wars has had no shortage of breakout alien stars over the decades--from Chewbacca in the original trilogy to Grogu from The Mandalorian--but in Star Wars: Galactic Racer, that honor belongs to Biddy Blas. Who is Biddy Blas?
body: Performing under the name "The Spectacular Tw*t" Charles Crowley, Summers-Calvert has popped up in multiple pro wrestling promotions, including a recent appearance in Ring of Honor. The actor and wrestler says he's been humbled by Biddy Blas's popularity since he was introduced in Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

"I could tell Biddy Blas was gonna be popular early on," Summers-Calvert said to Soundsphere. "Then I woke up the next day and he'd blown up a bit, and then the next day it kind of dawned on me that this isn’t normal."

Since then, Summers-Calvert says he has received a ton of messages, mentions, and even "Biddy Blas thirst traps" online. For the role, Summers-Calvert recalled that the audition called for a small man who was constantly on the edge and overcompensating, which convinced the pro wrestler to raise his pitch. The game directors liked it, but the role wasn't easy--especially when he had to perform his lines in the Star Wars language of Huttese. "I keep seeing online people talking about like cuteness aggression, and they love him so much they want to throw him at the wall," Summers-Calvert added.

articles.title: Abbott & Costello Join Forces With Kolchak the Night Stalker in Horror Crossover Special
articles.summary: It's been said before, but 2026 really is the year of the bizarre comic book crossover. On top of books like Batman/Superman/Weird Al: World's Weirdest, now Monstrous Books is bringing back legendary comedy duo Abbott & Costello for a new trio of horror-themed team-up specials.
body: Monstrous Books is releasing three new specials in all, with the other two team-ups being Abbott & Costello Meet the Morlocks and Abbott & Costello Meet Cthulu. These books mark the first new Abbott & Costello comics in more than 50 years.

Abbott & Costello Meet the Monsters #1 is written by James Aquilone, with art by Dave Acosta, colors by Zac Atkinson, letters by Taylor Esposito, and cover art by J.K. Woodward, Lukas Ketner, and Zac Atkinson.

"These six pages from Abbott & Costello Meet the Monsters #1 set the stage for the entire series," Aquilone tells IGN. "The story begins in 1943, with Bud and Lou serving in the Army. While on leave, the duo accidentally stumble through an experimental portal that sends them traveling through time."

articles.title: PlayStation Shadowdrops Saros Zenith Update With Boss Rush, New Game+ and Fancy Golden Crown Powerups
articles.summary: A new update for Saros dropped today, adding some new features to the hectic Housemarque shooter. New Carcosan Modifiers allow players to further tweak the challenge, a boss rush mode lets you compete on leaderboards, and Arjun gets a golden glow.
body: Zenith adds 10 new Trial Modifiers to increase the challenge level. One example is “Hostile Regeneration,” which allows you to stun larger enemies, but you have to get in and finish them with a melee strike before they recover.

The update also adds New Game+, which adds mysterious new nodes to the Armor Matrix back at Passage. You use these to move through Eclipse Layers, which ramp up the challenge with new rules and deadlier enemies.

During Eclipse Layers, Arjun dons a golden crown and his armor glows. The more trials you have active, the more it glows and the flashier his gilded attire gets. Wearing the crown also grants access to new story and lore entries called Visions.

Then there’s Overlord Rush, accessed via the primary unit in Passage. This is a training simulation boss rush mode that lets you take down the fiercest Saros enemies and compete for a place on global leaderboards.
points: A new update for Saros dropped today, adding some new features to the hectic Housemarque shooter.

articles.title: Star Wars Games Could Get More Interesting As Lucasfilm Looks Beyond The Big Studios
articles.summary: This year has seen the launch of two Star Wars games, with each one offering a new take on a galaxy far (far!) away. Bit Reactors' Star Wars Zero Company puts its best XCOM foot forward with an aggressive take on turn-based tactics, while Fuse Games' Star Wars Galactic Racer has been hailed for its…
body: "It very much is part of the strategy," Lucasfilm Games VP Douglas Reilly said to The Game Business Show. "Obviously, huge AAA games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy. But one of the great things about Star Wars is it has all kinds of other opportunities to tell stories in different genres. The goal has been to find the best partner to bring that experience to life inside the galaxy far, far away. And it doesn’t have to always be AAA; sometimes it can be AA, and it’s really about the experience that we’re delivering and the fantasy we’re fulfilling."

Reilly added that Lucasfilm Games wants to be more flexible in choosing who it partners with to create more Star Wars titles, and some of those studios will "surprise" people when they're eventually revealed. As Reilly put it, Lucasfilm Games isn't looking for a "top five publisher," but rather teams that can meet their expectations for a high-quality title.

articles.title: PlayStation 6 RAM and Storage Alone May Cost $680, According to Leaker
articles.summary: The PlayStation 6 hasn't even been announced yet, but little rumors pop up now and then that add speculation on what to expect from Sony's next-gen console. The latest is a shocking claim that the RAM and storage configuration of the console will cost more than the entirety of the PS5.
body: Today's rumor comes via a long thread about next-gen hardware on NeoGaf, where known leaker Kepler_L2 simply said: "RAM + NAND alone is over $680." This was in response to another commenter who optimistically hoped that the console would come in at around $680. But, if Kepler_L2's numbers are right, and you should take them with a grain of salt, there's little chance of that happening.

This isn't the first time that Kepler_L2 has shared the leaked manufacturing cost of the PS6. Back in March, elsewhere on NeoGaf, they suggested the BoM (Bill of Materials) for the PS6 would be $760. But, due to the ongoing RAM crisis, they amended that estimate by saying the cost has gone up by around $200 in June. That would leave an estimated BoM of $960, which doesn't take into consideration additional costs like R&D, marketing and shipping. Keep in mind, though, that Sony has yet to say anything official about the price of PS6.
points: The PlayStation 6 hasn't even been announced yet, but little rumors pop up now and then that add speculation on what to expect from Sony's next-gen console.

articles.title: Resident Evil 7 Dev Reveals the Game’s Last of Us Inspiration and Troubled Development
articles.summary: It's hard to believe that it has almost been a decade since Capcom reinvented Resident Evil with the seventh mainline game in the series. In the fallout of Resident Evil 6, it seemed like the once great horror franchise was done for good, but then the developer delivered something of a miracle with…
body: In response to a long thread about Resident Evil 7: Biohazard, former Capcom manager Miguel Corti penned his own, even longer, thread about the behind-the-scenes story of how the bold reinvention of the series came to be. If you have the patience, you can read through the entire 66-post thread, which somehow touches on everything from Call of Duty and The Last of Us to more Leon Kennedy.

According to Corti, the original concept for Resident Evil 7 wasn't as drastic as the final product. Most importantly, it wouldn't be a soft reboot but would instead pick up after the events of the much-derided Resident Evil 6. "What was going to be the solution for RE7?" wrote Corti, "More Leon and more Umbrella connections!" There was apparently even talk at some point of Rebecca Chambers and Jill Valentine returning as well. As for why Capcom would even want to continue with Resident Evil 6 's style, Corti stated that the game "sold like gangbusters" despite poor reviews.
points: It's hard to believe that it has almost been a decade since Capcom reinvented Resident Evil with the seventh mainline game in the series.

articles.title: Arc Raiders player numbers hit a six-month high following the release of the extraction shooter's huge Frozen Trails update
articles.summary: Arc Raiders is still going strong almost a year after finding viral success, and it's all thanks to Embark Studios' one-two-punch strategy of launching a huge new update, Frozen Trails, to coincide with a free weekend.
body: Arc Raiders' Frozen Trails update upgraded the extraction shooter to version 2.0 earlier this month - 8th October - and quickly led to a surge in Steam players interested in its tense PvEvP shootouts. A new report from Alinea Analytics ' Rhys Elliott now claims a similar resurgence took place across all platforms where the game's available.

According to the report, Arc Raiders' comeback peaked with a whopping 1.7m daily players jumping in on the 14th of October, its biggest player count in six months, mostly driven by the aforementioned update. What's perhaps most interesting is that player numbers actually peaked just after the game's free trial weekend ended on 12th October - though around 150,000 new looters reportedly joined the robo-infested wasteland during that weekend period.

Both events coincided with the game's steepest discount yet, slashing its price tag by 50% to $19.99. In the three days after the free trial, Arc Raiders sold another 150,000 copies and brought home roughly $3m, not counting microtransactions, per the report.

articles.title: Star Trek Actor Breaks Silence on Starfleet Academy's Cancellation
articles.summary: Star Trek 's immediate future doesn’t look particularly bright. The two remaining Star Trek series, Strange New Worlds and Starfleet Academy, are both ending soon with nothing else in the immediate pipeline.
body: Longtime Star Trek actor Robert Picardo, who played the AI hologram The Doctor in multiple shows and movies in the franchise, offered incisive comments about the recent cancellation of Starfleet Academy.

“Even though I think the quality of our show was great, we were kind of killed in the cradle, and I believe part of it is the present political moment in our culture that diversity, that all of Star Trek’s core values are now out of fashion temporarily,” Picardo said in an interview with TrekMovie.

“We see diversity under attack, and therefore Star Trek is under attack because that’s what Star Trek’s always been about,” he continued. “So hopefully, whenever they create the next Star Trek movie and Star Trek show, they’ll remember what it was that made Star Trek special, and that present weather conditions in politics will change, and Star Trek once again will emerge with all of its values intact. That’s what I believe and I hope for. But right now, you know, the feeling has been a little grim recently.”

articles.title: PlayStation founder Ken Kutaragi says discs became "metaphor for 'owning' games", and that upset at their discontinuation is a "mentality issue"
articles.summary: Ken Kutaragi, the founder of PlayStation and architect of the first three PlayStation consoles, has said that people being upset about Sony's discontinuation of game discs is probably a "mentality issue".
body: Kutaragi was speaking to Video Games Chronicle at the Game Republic New Horizons event, where he said: "I understand that physical discs have become a metaphor for 'owning' games. I really understand that mentality... But nobody thinks [physical media] is necessary for a networked device like a smartphone, for example, because people feel that they will keep their content. So it's a mentality.
"I really understand [why some people are upset]," he added, "but I don't think it's economically reasonable. Maybe it's a mentality issue."

Kutaragi retired from PlayStation in June 2007, shortly after the PlayStation 3's European release, so he's been out of the company for a while. Two generations of consoles have passed since he left, though I'm sure he has close ties to Sony and people working there still. "I'm not the CEO at PlayStation any more," he noted in the interview, "but we still have some common [view points]."

Maybe Sony is pushing towards an all-digital device, he remarked, in a similar way that we see smartphones and other devices. "Maybe that's how those people are thinking," he said. "But this has caused some friction with game enthusiasts."

Kempshall's newest novel takes the same grounded, real-world historical approach to unpack Star Wars' ships, weapons, and the psychology of warfare as he did in his previous foundational text on the Galactic Empire, Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire.​ In Star Pilots, Kempshall delivers a gritty, authentic account of what it took to fight in the Galactic Civil War from behind a starfighter's controls. Wedge Antilles, a fan-favorite Rebel fighter ace from his first appearance in the original 1977 film, narrates this account-driven book and offers insight through unreleased interviews and New Republic archive data.

articles.title: Pokémon Skateboards Officially Launch, and Scalpers Are Already Buying Them Up
articles.summary: Oct. 17 marked the release of Santa Cruz skateboard blind bags containing illustrated decks of some of the Pokémon Trading Card Game's best art. Classic cards like the base-set Charizard and more modern cards like the " Moonbreon " from Evolving Skies are randomly packaged in these new products.
body: There are 30 decks in all, and three rare "chase" golden foil variant designs, of which only 500 exist in the world. The boards aren't just blown-up reproductions of their cardboard counterparts, though. The designs expand beyond the cards, usually in ways that capture the monster's elemental essence. The Blastoise skateboard, for example, is flush with water waves.

Much like their inspirations, the Santa Cruz blind bags are selling out immediately through a combination of eager fans and salivating scalpers. The skateboards normally retail for $139.99, but on resale sites like eBay or Facebook Marketplace, the prices quickly become exorbitant. On the low end, for less desirable designs, there are boards going for somewhere around $250. In the mid-range, for fan-favorite cards depicting Eeveelutions or starters, price tags hover around $1,500. The scarce chase boards, which depict a cacophony of multiple cards in a single picture, are listed between $5,000 and $9,000.
points: 17 marked the release of Santa Cruz skateboard blind bags containing illustrated decks of some of the Pokémon Trading Card Game's best art.

articles.title: Japanese acting union fights back against AI-generated voice use, proposing strict new guidelines, especially regarding the use of a deceased actor's voice
articles.summary: The Japan Actors Union has issued new rules, guidelines, and restrictions related to AI-generated voice use. This includes an outright ban on the replication of the voices of dead actors, unless the actor had authorised its use during their lifetime.
body: Per Automaton, these guidelines are meant to protect an industry that has been exposed to exploitation by generative AI. One example includes voice actor Kenjiro Tsuda (Jujutsu Kaisen and Chainsaw Man) taking Tiktok to court in an attempt to remove AI-generated voice imitations from the platform. He would go on to lose that case, but not without setting a precedent that a person's voice is subject to protection under publicity rights laws.

The second point, meanwhile, states that AI replications of an actor's work are to be counted as a new performance under the guidelines. This would mean royalties or compensation must be paid by AI companies to the actors involved.

Next up comes generative AI-powered translations, which takes an actor's performance and automatically changes it to another language. These must maintain the "artistic integrity" of the original performance, the guidelines state, and may not be used without permission in overseas regions.
points: The Japan Actors Union has issued new rules, guidelines, and restrictions related to AI-generated voice use.
This includes an outright ban on the replication of the voices of dead actors, unless the actor had authorised its use during their lifetime.

Oliver tests out The Crew Motorfest on Switch 2, while John has thoughts on Castlevania: Belmont's Curse.
